Hey Michael — thanks. Thu 8/28 13:30–14:00 PT works best for our team.

One more datapoint: our IT team enforces strict calendar SSO and strips some embedded URLs from third-party invites (we see that often with Meet). The earlier invite had a description where the join token ended with "...qXyZ" and then the link was split into two lines in the .ics; that caused our calendar UI to render a broken button.

Yes to Zoom fallback — if you can include the join URL explicitly in the email body (not only in the .ics) and reference a meeting ID/passcode we'll be solid.

Thanks — Sara

Looping in operational notes so we're all aligned.

Michael / Jordan — quick checklist before sending the new invite:
- Create meeting from michael@redwood.com (company calendar) so organizer metadata is Redwood and not a forwarded personal calendar.
- Include a Zoom bridge as the primary join link in the email body and in the .ics (some calendar systems will still show Meet; body link prevents click stripping).
- Paste the Zoom meeting ID and passcode in the description (e.g., Meeting ID: 987 654 3210, Passcode: Olive2025).
- Add a short fallback block: "If your calendar UI hides links, use the Zoom URL directly: https://zoom.us/j/9876543210".
- Attach a plain-text copy of the invite (zoom-bridge-template.txt) for fragile recipients.

I'll prepare the bridge and host the demo with Jordan. Michael — can you send the calendar invite from your Redwood account and confirm the organizer shows as "Redwood Inference"? If you want I can provision the Zoom bridge and send you the link.

Ben Carter
Sales — Redwood Inference
